plan.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a spread of angular speeds within the intended sub-rotation regime, especially where the drag torque remains a non-negligible fraction of the gravitational torque scale but does not stop motion immediately; negligible near omega≈0 and stronger at larger |omega|.

plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes all dissipative torque is strictly proportional to angular velocity, omitting the common speed-dependent increase of drag magnitude seen for bodies moving through air.
plan.baseline_assumption: The damping torque is purely linear viscous rotational damping over the whole sampled speed range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Quadratic aerodynamic drag acting against motion, producing an additional odd torque proportional to omega*|omega|.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the damping law rather than alter the restoring torque, because the benchmark already aims to cover both small and large angular deflections using the exact sinusoidal gravity term. The parent target mapping has a single damping gain: holding theta fixed, changing omega changes domega_dt only linearly through -(damping_coefficient/moment_of_inertia)*omega. Under ordinary laboratory conditions with a rigid pendulum moving through air, drag often grows faster than linearly with speed, so the child should show curvature in the omega-to-domega_dt relation. The distinguishing condition is to compare states with similar theta but different angular-speed magnitudes along observed trajectories, while mass, gravity, center_of_mass_distance, moment_of_inertia, and damping_coefficient are held fixed for a given system. Then the parent predicts a constant local slope with respect to omega, whereas the refined model predicts stronger opposition at larger |omega|. A single refit of the parent's existing parameters cannot reproduce both near-zero-speed weak damping and higher-speed stronger damping across those conditions, because changing damping_coefficient only rescales one linear odd term and cannot create speed-dependent curvature. This contrast is scientifically admissible in the stated sub-rotation regime so long as trajectories include moderate speeds; if all sampled motion stays very close to omega=0, the refinement would be weakly observable.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when quadratic drag is already non-negligible relative to linear damping at moderate sub-rotation speeds and the surrounding flow does not relax instantaneously compared with the swing timescale, so repeated high-speed passages leave a transient wake memory.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the effect appears as small but systematic history-dependent variation in deceleration during moderate-speed passages; in holdout with larger-amplitude but still sub-rotation trajectories, the same memory mechanism strengthens because wake buildup is larger, extending the contrast without changing the underlying physics.
plan.continuation_path: Fast environmental relaxation or vanishing coupling of drag to the environmental state recovers the parent law with a constant quadratic drag coefficient.
plan.promotion_reason: A history-dependent aerodynamic environment cannot be represented by the current instantaneous states theta and omega alone; a single additional state is needed to store the lagged flow or wake intensity that modulates drag.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes quadratic aerodynamic drag responds instantaneously to angular speed with a fixed coefficient, omitting finite relaxation of the surrounding flow and wake that can make drag depend on recent motion history.
plan.baseline_assumption: The existing quadratic drag coefficient is treated as a constant, memoryless property of the pendulum-environment interaction.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-time wake or boundary-layer adaptation around the moving pendulum creates a lagged aerodynamic state that modulates the strength of quadratic drag.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the memoryless-drag assumption rather than adding an unrelated force. The parent target mapping is domega_dt = f(theta, omega) with one shared quadratic-drag scale, so if two observed samples have the same theta and omega they must have the same predicted angular acceleration. That is a fixed-environment shortcut. A child with one additional aerodynamic-memory state would change the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory, because domega_dt would then depend on both instantaneous motion and recent history through the modulated drag. The concrete contrast is obtained by varying initial deflection and damping-dominated decay history while holding the instantaneous pair (theta, omega) approximately matched during later passages: after a recent high-speed sweep, the child can show stronger deceleration than after a quieter history, whereas the parent with a single refitted parameter set cannot reproduce different accelerations at the same observed theta and omega. This is scientifically admissible when speeds are high enough that quadratic drag matters but still below full rotation, and when aerodynamic relaxation is not effectively instantaneous. The limitation is that if the wake relaxation time is extremely short compared with the swing period, the effect collapses back to the parent and may be too weak to identify.

The child would instead introduce an interaction between theta and wake_intensity, so large-excursion states show additional restoring softening beyond what the same wake level causes near small excursion. This is scientifically admissible because aerodynamic normal-force effects generally depend on orientation relative to the flow and therefore need not remain proportional to a wake-only scalar. The effect is observable only when both wake_excess and deflection are appreciable; near small angles or wake_intensity near 1 the refinement collapses toward the parent and may be hard to distinguish. A single refit of the parent gain cannot reproduce both weak softening at small |theta| and stronger softening at large |theta| under the same wake_intensity because its mapping is separable in sin(theta) times a wake-only factor.

response_change.parent_relation: The wake-softened restoring term scales as sin(theta) divided by a wake-only factor, so at fixed wake_intensity the ratio of restoring acceleration to sin(theta) is independent of deflection amplitude.
response_change.child_relation: Make the wake-induced restoring softening itself amplitude dependent, so the effective reduction grows with both wake_intensity and deflection magnitude; at fixed wake_intensity, larger |theta| experiences disproportionately more restoring weakening than smaller |theta|.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding wake_intensity and omega near the same values across samples, the child predicts a smaller-magnitude restoring contribution at larger |theta| than the parent's single wake gain allows, producing extra flattening of the acceleration-versus-theta curve at large deflection.

diagnostic_groups.name: grav_scale
diagnostic_groups.role: baseline gravitational angular-acceleration scale

diagnostic_groups.name: wake_excess
diagnostic_groups.role: amount of motion-induced wake above ambient that can activate aerodynamic softening

diagnostic_groups.name: deflection_strength
diagnostic_groups.role: bounded measure of angular excursion size that is even in theta and zero at small deflection

contract.activation_condition: Observable when wake_intensity exceeds ambient by order-unity or modestly above and trajectories reach moderate to large deflections, so 1 - cos(theta) is non-negligible while remaining below full-rotation energy.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate versus larger deflection segments at similar wake_intensity already reveal extra flattening of restoring acceleration; in holdout, the same interaction extends to stronger wake episodes without changing sign symmetry or periodicity.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the amplitude-dependent softening coefficient tends to zero, or in the small-angle limit theta -> 0 where 1 - cos(theta) vanishes to leading order.
contract.domain_mechanism: deflection-dependent wake softening of gravitational restoring torque
contract.scientific_mechanism: At larger deflections the body presents a different effective incidence to the surrounding separated flow, so the same wake state produces a stronger normal-force-induced reduction of restoring torque than near the bottom position.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the restoring coefficient now varies with theta through a bounded nonlinear state function, changing the curvature of the target mapping rather than simply rescaling it.
contract.assumption_before: Wake-induced restoring softening depends only on wake excess and uses one shared gain across all deflection amplitudes.
contract.assumption_after: Wake-induced restoring softening depends on wake excess and is strengthened at larger angular excursions through an amplitude-dependent coefficient.
contract.before_fragment: -(mass * gravity * center_of_mass_distance / moment_of_inertia) * sin(theta) / (1 + aerodynamic_stiffness_gain * Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0)) - (damping_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * omega - (quadratic_drag_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * wake_intensity * omega * Abs(omega)
contract.after_fragment: -(mass * gravity * center_of_mass_distance / moment_of_inertia) * sin(theta) / (1 + aerodynamic_stiffness_gain * (1 + amplitude_softening_gain * (1 - cos(theta))) * Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0)) - (damping_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * omega - (quadratic_drag_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * wake_intensity * omega * Abs(omega)
contract.parent_reduction: Set amplitude_softening_gain = 0, or take theta -> 0 so that 1 - cos(theta) -> 0 and the denominator reverts to the parent form to leading order.
contract.observable_signature: Compared at similar wake_intensity and omega, normalized restoring acceleration is no longer a function of wake_intensity alone: it decreases further with increasing deflection_strength = 1 - cos(theta), giving visibly more flattened acceleration-versus-theta behavior at large |theta| while matching the parent near small angles or wake_intensity near 1.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of aerodynamic_stiffness_gain in the parent cannot simultaneously match weak softening at small |theta| and stronger softening at large |theta| under the same wake_intensity, because the parent mapping is separable as sin(theta) times a wake-only denominator and therefore lacks the required theta-wake interaction.

range_suggestions.amplitude_softening_gain: positive and small to moderate; zero recovers the parent law, while order-unity values give observable extra wake softening at moderate to large |theta| without reversing the restoring torque
